data.description:
# Remote access: backend rejects WebSocket connections from non-localhost origins

## Problem statement

Running the web demo in dev mode on a host and opening it from a **remote**
browser leaves the embedded terminal stuck on `[Backend not available]`. The
backend rejects the WebSocket upgrade because the browser's `Origin` header is
the remote host address, which is not in the default `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`
(`localhost,127.0.0.1`). The terminal's on-screen guidance is also misleading:
it tells the operator to run `cd web && npm start` (production) even though dev
mode is started with `npm run dev:web -- --host`.

## Users

- **Remote demo operator (primary)** — a developer who runs the web demo on a
  build/workstation machine and opens it from another device (LAN or Tailscale)
  via `npm run dev:web -- --host`. Wants the embedded terminal to work without
  hand-editing environment variables.
- **Local developer (secondary)** — runs the same command on `localhost` and
  must not see any behaviour change or weakened origin security.

Example user stories:

- As a remote demo operator, I want `npm run dev:web -- --host` to start a
  backend that accepts WebSocket connections from the machine's network
  hostnames/IPs, so the in-browser terminal works from another device.
- As a local developer, I want localhost-only usage to remain restricted to
  `localhost`/`127.0.0.1`, so the origin restriction still protects the PTY
  backend from arbitrary websites.
- As an operator whose backend is genuinely down, I want the terminal message
  to show the correct dev command, so I know how to fix it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. With the dev stack started via `npm run dev:web -- --host`, a browser on a
   remote device (using the host's LAN/Tailscale hostname or IP) can open the
   WebSocket terminal — the backend logs `ACCEPTED` (not `403 Forbidden`) and
   the terminal connects.
2. The dev start script configures the backend's allowed origins to include the
   host's own network hostnames/IPs (in addition to `localhost`/`127.0.0.1`),
   without the operator setting `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` manually.
3. Localhost-only connect behaviour is unchanged: an unrelated origin (e.g.
   `http://evil.example.com`) is still rejected with `403` in both dev and
   production.
4. The `[Backend not available]` terminal message displays the correct dev-mode
   startup command (`npm run dev:web -- --host`) instead of `cd web && npm start`.
5. `web/README.md` documents remote-access usage and the derived
   `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` behaviour (Environment Variables / Troubleshooting).
6. A test asserts the origin-allowance behaviour for a non-localhost host that
   is part of the allowed set (unit test of `isOriginAllowed`/allowed-origin
   derivation), and an unrelated origin remains rejected.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Keep the production default (`web` `npm start` / container run) secure:
  `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` must continue to default to `localhost,127.0.0.1`.
- No new runtime dependency for production; dev-only helper code is acceptable.
- Must work on Linux dev hosts (macOS desirable, Windows best-effort) as the
  project's dev scripts are Unix-oriented (e.g. `concurrently`).
- The WebSocket proxy path (Vite → backend) must keep forwarding the browser
  `Origin`, so the backend decision remains authoritative.

## Existing state

- `web/server/index.ts` — `DEFAULT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS = "localhost,127.0.0.1"`;
  `isOriginAllowed()` matches `url.hostname` exactly against the comma list;
  rejects with `403 Forbidden` on upgrade. No wildcard support.
- Root `package.json` — `dev:web` runs `npm run build && npm run build --prefix
  web && concurrently ... "npm start --prefix web" "npm run dev --prefix web"`.
  It does **not** set `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`; vite's `dev` script already includes
  `--host`.
- `web/vite.config.ts` — forwards `/ws/*` upgrades to the backend on the
  discovered `.port`, preserving the browser `Origin`.
- `web/src/terminal.ts` — on max reconnect attempts shows
  `Ensure the backend server is running: cd web && npm start`.
- Reproduced: backend log shows
  `REJECTED origin=http://100.106.5.111:5174 403 Forbidden` when accessed over
  Tailscale; a `localhost` origin returns `101 Switching Protocols`.

## Desired change

- Extend the dev start script (`dev:web`, or a documented sibling such as
  `dev:web:host`) so the backend is launched with `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` containing
  `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, and the host's detected network hostnames/IPs.
  Detection should be a small Node helper (cross-platform, no shell-only
  parsing) so `npm run dev:web -- --host` "just works" remotely.
- Correct the terminal's `[Backend not available]` guidance to the dev command.
- Add/adjust tests for allowed-origin derivation and rejection of unrelated
  origins.
- Update `web/README.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `package.json` — update the `dev:web` script to inject `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`
  (dev-only); possibly add a helper invocation for host detection.
- `scripts/` (repo root, new helper) — e.g. `allowed-origins.mjs` that prints
  `localhost,127.0.0.1,<hostname>,<network IPs>` for the current host.
- `web/server/index.ts` — only if wildcard/host-name derivation needs a backend
  tweak; otherwise unchanged.
- `web/src/terminal.ts` — fix the `[Backend not available]` guidance text.
- `web/test/server.test.ts` — add/adjust origin-allowance tests.
- `web/README.md` — remote-access + `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` documentation.
- `web/package.json` — if a web-local helper/script is preferred over a root one.

## Related work

- `TF-0MLXBIH6E0U1Z8QT` — Fix Tone.js AudioContext and WebSocket connection
  errors in dev mode (completed; introduced the reconnect/backoff UX and the
  `[Backend not available]` message, but did not address remote origins).
- `TF-0MLX7CEKN122VEPV` — Web Server & Project Infrastructure (completed;
  established `web/` dev/build/start scripts and `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (documented):** the operator is willing for the dev backend to
  trust the host's own network hostnames/IPs; production default stays strict.
- **Risk — over-permissive dev origins:** auto-allowing all host IPs widens
  the accepted set beyond localhost. Mitigation: dev-only injection; unrelated
  origins still rejected; production `npm start` unchanged.
- **Risk — unreliable host detection:** multi-interface/Tailscale hosts may
  have several addresses; the helper must enumerate all and keep the list
  tolerant (ignore failures). Fallback to `localhost,127.0.0.1`.
- **Risk — Windows portability:** `VAR=value cmd` prefixes are Unix-only.
  Mitigation: prefer a helper that writes env via `concurrently` config or a
  Node launcher; note Windows as best-effort.
- **Scope creep:** any desire to make wildcard origins configurable in
  production or to auto-open firewall ports is out of scope — capture as a
  separate work item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "How should remote origins be enabled?" — **Recommended:** update the dev
  start script to derive and pass the host's own hostnames/IPs to
  `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (keeps production strict) rather than allowing all origins.
  Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — proceeding with the recommended approach as a
  documented assumption; producer may redirect to a dedicated
  `dev:web:host` script or a wildcard dev mode.
- Q: "Should the misleading `[Backend not available]` text be corrected too?"
  Answer: Yes — included in AC 4 (clearly implied by the reported symptom).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **TF-0MM0W4YUZ0QF26DG** – Investigate and reduce latency of sound generation (completed)
- **TF-0MLXJ6JKK1L2QC10** – Improve intro and recap text formatting in CLI and web demo (completed)
- **TF-0MM1W2DX80RSXZNA** – Remove printf sentinel from demo terminal injection (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `standups/2026_10_05.md` — matched: access, add, addition, already, another (+159 more)
- `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` — matched: acceptance, add, adjust, already, auto (+137 more)
